result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_agg_degree_out()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get aggregate value from outdegree of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23776-L23906){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_agg_degree_out( agg, conditions=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Aggregate out-degree](/assets/graphs/get-agg-degree-out.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph with each node's out-degree in a badge: A 2, B 2, C 1, D 2, E 0. The card sums them to 7 over 5 nodes and gives the mean out-degree 1.4." width="100%"} Computes a single aggregate statistic from the outdegree values of all nodes in a directed graph. Useful for summarizing the outdegree distribution or analyzing filtered node subsets. Each node's out-degree is found with `get_out_degree()` (parallel edges each count, edge weights are ignored), the nodes are optionally filtered with `conditions=`, and the remaining values are reduced to one number. Typical questions it answers: - how many outgoing links does a typical node have (`"mean"` or `"median"`)? - are there nodes with no outgoing edges at all (`"min"` of `0`)? - do nodes in one group send more links than another (compare `"mean"` with different `conditions=`)? All nodes in the graph are considered; any node selection is ignored, so use `conditions=` to restrict the set. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [agg]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Aggregation function to apply. Must be one of: - `"sum"`: sum of all outdegrees (equal to the number of edges when no `conditions=` are given) - `"min"`: minimum outdegree - `"max"`: maximum outdegree - `"mean"`: mean outdegree - `"median"`: median outdegree (the mean of the two middle values when the number of nodes is even) [conditions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Filter function that takes a node object and returns `True` to include the node in the aggregation. If `None`, all nodes are included. The node object has `id`, `label`, and `attributes` properties; `attributes` is a dictionary, or `None` for a node without attributes, so a safe filter looks like `lambda n: (n.attributes or {}).get("kind") == "gene"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The computed aggregate outdegree value. Returns `0.0` if no nodes match the conditions. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or if `agg=` is not a valid aggregation function. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_agg_degree_in`) : The same summary for in-degree. [](`~get_agg_degree_total`) : The same summary for total degree; also works on undirected graphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every edge has exactly one source, so in a random directed graph with 20 nodes and 35 edges the mean out-degree is `35 / 20`, or `1.75`, the same as the mean in-degree: ::: {#c62f3380 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_gnm_graph(20, 35, seed=23) graph.get_agg_degree_out('mean') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.75 ``` ::: ::: The median can differ from the mean when out-degrees are uneven: ::: {#59c48197 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_agg_degree_out('median') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1.5 ``` ::: ::: Passing `conditions=` restricts the aggregation to a subset of nodes. In this small citation network, `"cs"` papers cite other papers more often on average than `"bio"` papers do: ::: {#872a0dd1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} papers = ec.Graph(directed=True) for label, field in [ ("P1", "bio"), ("P2", "bio"), ("P3", "cs"), ("P4", "cs"), ("P5", "bio"), ("P6", "cs") ]: papers.add_node(label=label, field=field) for citing, cited in [ ("P2", "P1"), ("P3", "P1"), ("P4", "P1"), ("P4", "P2"), ("P5", "P3"), ("P6", "P5"), ("P6", "P1"), ]: papers.add_edge(citing, cited) { field: papers.get_agg_degree_out( "mean", conditions=lambda n: n.attributes["field"] == field ) for field in ["bio", "cs"] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'bio': 0.6666666666666666, 'cs': 1.6666666666666667} ``` ::: :::
